Users and permission profiles

Create and manage SATOM accounts and compose the permission profiles that decide exactly what each account may do, with a guard that never lets you remove the last administrator.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage profiles.manage users.view
📍 WhereSettings → Access & Identity → Users / Profiles (URL /settings/#tab-users, /settings/#tab-profiles; also /users/ and /profiles/)

What is it?#

Every person who signs in to SATOM has a user account, and every account is assigned exactly one permission profile. The profile is a named set of granular permissions (for example View protection, Apply network, Manage users) and it is the only thing that decides what the user can see and do. Three system profiles ship with SATOM — readonly, operator and admin — and administrators can compose any number of custom profiles on top of them.

What does it do?#

  • Users lists every account with its profile, creation date, last login and status, and lets an administrator add, enable/disable, re-profile and delete accounts, reset a local account's password, clear its two-factor authentication and unlock it after failed sign-ins. Holders of users.view alone see the same list read-only.
  • Profiles lists every profile with its type (System / Custom), the Effective role it behaves like, how many permissions it grants and how many users carry it. Custom profiles can be created, edited, cloned and deleted; system profiles can be viewed and cloned.
  • An anti-lockout guard refuses any change that would leave SATOM without at least one active user who can manage both users and profiles.
  • Nobody grants more than they hold. A user who can manage users or profiles but is not a full administrator cannot assign or create a profile wider than their own, cannot reset the password or clear the 2FA of an account that holds more than they do, cannot add a permission they do not hold to a profile, and cannot edit the profile they are assigned to. Moving yourself to a narrower profile is allowed; a wider one is not.
  • Every change is written to the Audit Log.

The full list of permission keys, with what each one unlocks, is in Permissions.

Requirements#

  • To manage users you need users.manage; to manage profiles you need profiles.manage. A fresh install seeds one administrator account, admin, on the admin profile (see First login).
  • Directory accounts (Active Directory / LDAP / RADIUS) are not created here: they are created automatically at first sign-in or imported under Settings → Authentication. Once they exist they appear in the Users list and are managed exactly like local accounts.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

  • Users (/users/ and Settings → Access & Identity → Users): the list opens with users.view or users.manage; every action (add, enable/disable, change profile, reset password, clear 2FA, unlock, delete) requires users.manage. With users.view only, the page shows Read-only view instead of Add User, the Actions column is hidden, and the sidebar shows a Users entry above Settings. With neither key, /users/ returns 403 Forbidden. The Access & Identity group of Settings is shown only to users.manage holders.
  • Profiles (/profiles/ and Settings → Access & Identity → Profiles): every route requires profiles.manage. Without it, /profiles/ and every profile action return 403 Forbidden, and the Settings → Profiles tab is not shown: a custom profile with users.manage but not profiles.manage sees Users but no Profiles tab.
  • In the shipped profiles only Administrator holds users.view, users.manage and profiles.manage; the last two are administrative capabilities.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: users.view now opens a read-only user list, the Users table gained Reset password, Clear 2FA and Unlock, passwords need at least 12 characters, and the Profiles tab requires profiles.manage.

The three system profiles#

Profile Shown as What it grants
readonly Read Only "Read-only access to every section. Cannot change anything." The view keys of every area: monitoring.view, protection.view, network.view, operations.view, backups.view, registry.view, audit.view, appliances.view.
operator Operator "Read everything plus manage appliances, protection, network, backups and operations. No user or registry administration." Everything in readonly plus advisor.use, backups.create, backups.restore, protection.edit, protection.apply, network.edit, network.apply, operations.apply, operations.template_save, operations.template_apply, appliances.edit, appliances.apply.
admin Admin "Full access, including user and profile administration." Every permission key in the catalog.

System profiles are re-synchronised from the code every time SATOM starts. When a release adds a new permission key, admin gains it automatically. This is also why system profiles are read-only: an edit would be overwritten at the next restart.

Permission areas#

The profile editor groups the catalog into twelve areas, in this order: Monitoring, Web Protection, Network, Operations, Backups, API Registry, Audit Log, Appliances, Studio, Users, Profiles, Scout (AI assistant). Keys marked with a shield icon (tooltip Administrative capability) are the sensitive ones: operations.template_approve, appliances.view_maintenance, studio.python_console, studio.plugin_studio, studio.lua_studio, users.manage, profiles.manage and advisor.configure. The icon is informational; it does not restrict who can tick the box.

How to use#

Open Settings and expand Access & Identity, then choose Users or Profiles. The same panels are also available as stand-alone pages at /users/ (sidebar → Administrator → Users, in the Global and FortiADC workspaces) and /profiles/.

Share apps and Wiki articles with a group#

Administrator → Access → Groups keeps named sets of users (users.manage). Python Studio apps are shared with groups or with people, and a Wiki article can be limited to groups: add a colleague to a group and they get every app and article of that group. New group → name, description, members → Save. A group an app is shared with cannot be deleted until it is removed from the app (the message names the apps). The Wiki articles column counts the articles naming each group; deleting such a group is allowed and leaves those articles closed (author and Wiki moderators only), never open to everyone. Until 2026-10-20 the Wiki kept groups of its own; the upgrade merged them here (same name in any case = one group).

Confine a profile to some ADOMs#

  1. Open the profile (Profiles → the profile's name). System profiles cannot be edited: clone one first.
  2. In the ADOMs card tick the ADOMs this profile may work in. With none ticked it may work in every ADOM, which is what every profile had before.
  3. Click Save permissions. The ADOMs column of the profile list shows the result (All, or one badge per ADOM).

What a confined profile gets:

  • The ADOM switcher and the sidebar list only its ADOMs. Opening any other ADOM — by link, URL or X-ADOM header — is refused with Your profile does not include the … ADOM (403 for API callers).
  • Its Global console is the union of its ADOMs: appliance lists and pages, jobs, change requests (one that also names a device outside its ADOMs is not shown), Sentinel, certificates, reports, metrics and the dashboard tiles.
  • The database tools and Global ADOM Assets are refused, because they read every ADOM. Script Library database fields still work: SATOM adds the ADOM filter to them.
  • A confined administrator can only create, edit and assign profiles within its own ADOMs, never an unconfined one, and cannot reset the password or clear the 2FA of an account wider than itself.

Background work (scheduled actions, the scheduler) is not a session and keeps acting on the whole fleet.

Add a user#

  1. On Users, click Add User.
  2. Enter Username, Password (at least 12 characters) and Confirm Password.
  3. Pick a Profile. readonly is preselected; system profiles are suffixed " — system".
  4. Click Create User. The flash reads "User <name> created."

Change a user's profile#

  1. In the user's row click the badge icon (tooltip Change Profile).
  2. In the Change Profile dialog pick the new profile and click Save Profile.
  3. The flash reads "<name> is now on profile “<profile>”." The new permissions apply from the user's next request.

Disable or re-enable a user#

Click the pause icon (Disable) or play icon (Enable) in the user's row. A disabled account cannot sign in; the login page tells it "This account is disabled." Enabling a directory account that is pending approval is how you approve it.

Reset a user's password#

Shown only for local accounts; directory accounts change their password in the directory.

  1. In the user's row click the key icon (tooltip Reset password).
  2. In the Reset password dialog enter the new password (at least 12 characters) twice and click Set password.
  3. The flash reads "Password for <name> reset successfully." The user signs in with the new password; the change is audited as user.reset_password.

Clear a user's two-factor authentication#

Use this when a user has lost their authenticator. The phone icon (tooltip Clear 2FA) appears only for accounts with two-factor authentication enabled.

  1. Click Clear 2FA and confirm "Clear two-factor authentication for '<name>'? They will sign in with their password only until they enrol again."
  2. The flash reads "Two-factor authentication cleared for <name>." The secret and the backup codes are removed (audited as user.clear_2fa). The user can enrol again under Settings → My account.

Unlock an account#

After failed sign-ins the Status column shows a warning badge: N failed while the counter is running, Locked once the account is locked out.

  1. In the user's row click the open-lock icon (tooltip Unlock) and confirm "Clear the sign-in lockout of '<name>'?"
  2. The flash reads "Sign-in lockout cleared for <name>." The failed-attempt counter and the lock are cleared (audited as user.unlock, with the previous values).

Unlock changes nothing else: a disabled or pending-approval account stays disabled until you click Enable.

Delete a user#

Click the trash icon (Delete) and confirm "Permanently delete user '<name>'? This cannot be undone."

On your own row, Disable, Change Profile and Delete are replaced by Current user: you cannot disable, re-profile or delete yourself from this table. Unlock, Reset password and Clear 2FA still appear there when they apply.

Find users#

Type in Search users… to filter by any visible text, or choose a role in the All Roles filter (Admin, Operator, Read Only). Filtering happens in the browser. Directory accounts carry a badge with their source (for example LDAP); your own account carries You.

Create a custom profile#

  1. On Profiles, click New Profile.
  2. Enter a Profile name (required, unique, case-insensitive) and an optional Description, then click Create & set permissions.
  3. On the profile page, tick the permissions the profile should grant. Use Select all / Clear all to start from either end.
  4. Click Save permissions. The flash reads "Profile “<name>” updated."

Start from an existing profile#

Click the Clone icon on any profile, system or custom. SATOM creates "<name> copy" (or "<name> copy 2", "copy 3" … if that name is taken) with the same permissions and opens it for editing.

View or edit a profile#

Click the eye icon (system profile, View permissions) or the pencil icon (custom profile, Edit permissions). System profiles open read-only with the note "System profiles are managed automatically and shown read-only."

Delete a custom profile#

Click the trash icon and confirm "Delete profile '<name>'? This cannot be undone." The button is disabled while users are still assigned to the profile; reassign them first.

Configuration#

User fields#

Field Description Required Example
Username Sign-in name. Must not already exist. Yes jsmith
Password Local password, 12 to 1024 characters (length only, no character-class rule); stored as a scrypt hash. A shorter password is refused. Yes —
Confirm Password Must match Password when filled. Yes (in the form) —
Profile The permission profile. Defaults to readonly. No operator

Profile fields#

Field Description Required Example
Profile name / Name Unique name (case-insensitive), up to 64 characters. Yes WAF Editor
Description Free text shown under the name in the Profiles table. No Edits WAF profiles, cannot push
Permissions One checkbox per key in the catalog, grouped by area. A new profile starts with none. No View protection + Edit protection

Profiles table columns#

Column Meaning
Profile Name, description and an admin-capable badge when the profile holds both users.manage and profiles.manage.
Type System or Custom.
Effective role Admin if the profile grants users.manage; otherwise Operator if it grants any key that implies the config_write gate (edit/apply protection or network, run operations, the template keys, edit/run appliances); otherwise Read Only — even if it grants, for example, backups.create or registry.edit.
Permissions Number of keys granted.
Users Number of accounts on the profile.

Example#

🧪Example — A WAF editor who can stage but not push

  1. Profiles → New Profile, name WAF Editor, description Stages web-protection changes for review.
  2. Tick View monitoring, View protection, Edit protection, View appliances and View audit log. Leave Apply protection unticked.
  3. Save permissions. The table shows Effective role Operator (the profile grants a change permission) and 5 granted.
  4. Users → Add User jdoe, Profile WAF Editor, Create User.

jdoe can now author web-protection changes but cannot push them to an appliance, and cannot see Settings administration, users or profiles.

Result#

  • The change takes effect on the user's next request: permissions are read from the assigned profile on every request, not cached in the session.
  • Each action writes one audit entry: user.create, user.profile.set (with from and to), user.enabled.set (with state), user.reset_password, user.clear_2fa, user.unlock, user.delete, profile.create, profile.update and profile.clone (with the permission list or source), profile.delete.
  • Saving a custom profile also updates the legacy role label (Admin / Operator / Read Only) of every user on it, which drives the role badges, the Operators counter and the All Roles filter. The Admins counter counts admin-capable users (those who can manage both users and profiles), the same set the anti-lockout guard protects.

Troubleshooting#

"Refused: that change would remove the last administrator (no remaining user could manage users AND profiles)."#

Possible causes - You moved the last admin-capable user to a profile without users.manage or profiles.manage. - You removed one of those two permissions from the custom profile that all admin-capable users share.

Solution 1. First give a second, active user a profile with both permissions (for example admin). 2. Then repeat the change.

Verification On Profiles, at least one profile with users assigned shows the admin-capable badge, and at least one of those users is Active.

"Cannot delete the last remaining administrator." / "Cannot disable the last remaining administrator."#

Possible causes The account is the only active user who can manage both users and profiles.

Solution Give another active account an admin-capable profile, then delete or disable this one.

Verification The delete/disable succeeds with "User <name> deleted." / "User <name> disabled."

"You cannot delete your own account." / "You cannot change your own account status."#

Possible causes You tried to act on your own account (only possible by posting directly; the table hides the buttons on your row).

Solution Ask another administrator to do it.

"“<name>” is assigned to N user(s). Reassign them first."#

Possible causes The profile still has users.

Solution Use Change Profile on each of its users, then delete the profile. The Users column on Profiles shows when it reaches 0.

"A profile named “<name>” already exists."#

Possible causes Profile names are unique regardless of case: WAF editor clashes with WAF Editor.

Solution Choose another name, or clone and rename.

"System profiles are managed automatically and cannot be edited."#

Possible causes You tried to save a system profile.

Solution Clone it and edit the copy, then assign the copy to users.

"Username <name> already exists." / "Passwords do not match." / "The password must be at least 12 characters."#

Solution Pick another username, retype both password fields, or choose a password of 12 to 1024 characters.

A user is told "Too many failed attempts — account temporarily locked. Try again later."#

Possible causes Ten consecutive failed sign-ins lock the account for 15 minutes, regardless of source address.

Solution 1. An administrator clicks Unlock in the user's row (see Unlock an account), or the user waits 15 minutes; a successful sign-in then clears the counter. 2. If no administrator can sign in, a root operator on the SATOM node can run sudo satom execute admin unlock <username>. It clears the lockout only; a disabled account stays disabled. The command writes an Audit Log entry with user cli/root.

Verification The Locked badge is gone and the user signs in.

Nobody can sign in as an administrator#

Solution On the SATOM node, as root: sudo satom execute admin reset-password <username>. The password is asked interactively (12 to 1024 characters, the same policy as the web forms) and never passed on the command line; the command also clears the lockout and re-enables the account, and writes an Audit Log entry with user cli/root. satom get user list shows who can log in.

Verification The account signs in with the new password.

A user sees "Forbidden" (403) on a page#

Possible causes Their profile lacks the permission the page needs.

Solution Look up the page in Permissions, then add the key to the user's custom profile, or move the user to a profile that has it.

Advanced#

Advanced How permissions are resolved
  • A profile stores granular keys (area.action). Most routes still check one of five legacy coarse keys (view, backup, config_write, registry_edit, user_manage). Holding any granular key listed for a coarse key grants that coarse key: for example any of Edit/Apply protection, Edit/Apply network, Run operations, the template keys or Edit/Run appliances grants config_write; Manage users grants user_manage. The mapping is in Permissions.
  • Because of that projection, granting one change permission (for example appliances.edit) also opens every page gated only on config_write. Compose custom profiles with that in mind.
  • A user with no profile (only possible for rows created before profiles existed, or if the assigned profile row disappears — the link is set to empty on delete) is treated as the system profile matching their legacy role, defaulting to readonly.
  • Unknown keys stored in a profile (for example a key removed in a later release) are ignored when the profile is read and dropped when it is saved.
Advanced Anti-lockout internals

"Admin-capable" means the user's effective permissions contain both users.manage and profiles.manage. Profile saves, user edits and profile changes are flushed first, the number of active admin-capable users is counted, and the transaction is rolled back if it is zero. Deleting or disabling a user checks the same count excluding that user. The same "admin-capable" set is used elsewhere: it selects the recipients of administrator notifications and gates the most privileged Plugin Studio and Lua Studio actions.

Advanced User routes

Every Users action is a POST under /users/<id>/ that requires users.manage: profile, toggle-active, reset-password (fields new_password and confirm_password; local accounts only), clear-2fa, unlock and delete. There is no rename route: the former /users/<id>/edit page and the legacy /users/<id>/role endpoint were removed in 2.11.0; use Change Profile to re-profile, and delete and re-create an account to rename it. Users manage their own password and two-factor authentication under Settings → My account.
